config.title: Remove Nth Node from End

intro.title: Remove Nth Node from End
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function to remove the nth node from the end of a singly linked list. You will learn the two-pointer technique, a core algorithm pattern for efficiently solving linked list lessons. The main constructs involved are linked list node objects, pointer manipulation, and basic JavaScript loops. By the end, you will understand how to traverse a list once to find and remove a target node.
intro.usecase: The 'remove nth node from end' pattern appears in UI components where users can delete items from ordered lists or sequences. For example, in a task management dashboard, users might remove the second-to-last completed task from a history panel without recalculating positions from the beginning. This algorithm efficiently handles deletion in navigation menus, playlist editors, or log viewers where direct access to the target position isn't available. Developers implement this when building interactive lists that require precise removal operations based on relative position rather than absolute indexes.

objectives: Construct a singly linked list data structure with nodes containing value and next pointer properties
Initialize two pointers to traverse the linked list for locating the target node from the end
Manipulate pointer positions to maintain a gap that isolates the nth node from the end
Apply pointer adjustments to remove the target node by updating the previous node's next reference
Configure edge case handling for scenarios such as removing the head node or invalid positions
Integrate the removal logic into a complete function that returns the modified linked list head

familyTeachingProfile.conceptBridge: Add a pointer mental model first: we can only move to next (or prev); we cannot jump by index.
familyTeachingProfile.visualMetaphor: Show node-to-node traversal; one step at a time along the chain.
